text:
alex: Heads-up: opened PR 1347 to add a new 'edge' subnet + PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2 and update TGW attachments. plan looks OK but I want a quick sanity check before apply: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1347 :wave:

maya: thanks. please don't apply yet — last time we saw intermittent 502s when endpoint service and route propagation happened out of order. can you paste the tf snippets?

alex: sure — here's the relevant part from modules/network/main.tf:

```hcl
resource "aws_subnet" "edge" {
  vpc_id     = var.vpc_id
  cidr_block = var.edge_subnet_cidr
  availability_zone = var.az
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { "k8s.io/role/elb" = "1" })
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_privatelink" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = var.endpoint_service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = [aws_subnet.edge.id]
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.pl_endpoint.id]
}

resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" "tgw_attach" {
  transit_gateway_id = var.tgw_id
  vpc_id             = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids         = [aws_subnet.edge.id]
  tags = var.common_tags
}
```

sam: looks normal, but TF may create the endpoint before the TGW attachment or vice versa. the real failure we've hit is route table assoc happening before propogation, creating a temporary blackhole for services behind the endpoint.

ryan: exact problem: when the aws_route that points to the tgw attachment is created while the attachment is still 'pending', the route shows up but traffic is dropped. adding an explicit dependency or using `depends_on = [aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach]` on the route resource fixes it. also `create_before_destroy` on subnets helped in a separate cutover.

alex: got it. the PR currently lets the module order handle it implicitly. i'll add `depends_on` to the aws_route resources that reference the tgw attachment and to the endpoint's subnet association.

maya: also FYI the plan shows the NAT GW getting replaced because of EIP rotation (we're rotating the eip pool). plan snippet:

```
  # aws_eip.edge_nat_eip must be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_eip" "edge_nat_eip" {
    ~ id = "eip-0123" -> (known after apply)
  }

  # aws_nat_gateway.edge_nat will be replaced because its eip changes
  ~ resource "aws_nat_gateway" "edge_nat" {
    ~ allocation_id = "eipalloc-abc" -> (known after apply)
  }
```

sam: replacing NAT GW in a busy AZ caused some ephemeral connectivity issues last rollout. recommend doing nat EIP rotation in a maintenance window or creating a new nat + switch routes gradually.

alex: plan: I'll split the PR into two smaller applies — 1) create subnet + privatelink + TGW attachment (with depends_on and a null_resource wait), 2) rotate EIPs and swap NAT routes in a follow-up. that should reduce blast radius.

maya: sounds good. i'll review the first PR today. can you add a null_resource with a local-exec that polls `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments` until state=="available"? small example:

```hcl
resource "null_resource" "wait_for_tgw_attach" {
  depends_on = [aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<EOT
for i in {1..30}; do
  state=$(aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=resource-id,Values=${aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach.id} --query "Attachments[0].State" --output text)
  if [ "$state" = "available" ]; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 10
done
exit 1
EOT
  }
}
```

ryan: +1 on wait, and add a small delay (30s) after available before creating routes to let AWS propagate. also run the apply in one AZ first (canary) as maya suggested.

infra-bot: terraform-plan-bot: Plan for PR 1347 completed successfully (no errors). See checks -> infra/terraform.

alex: thanks all — i'll push the split PR and add the explicit depends_on/null_resource. pinging @maya for review when ready :pray: 

maya: will do. remind me to run the canary apply during low traffic window. :white_check_mark:
